content: Twelve-dollar eggs while Lin "negotiates"? Appeasement feeds cartels the same way it feeds enemies. Food security IS national security. Her backroom tables starve soldiers' families. A commander secures supply lines — Lin surrenders them.

Twelve-dollar eggs and Stone's answer? More subpoenas! Twenty years, zero groceries delivered, zero ROI — both party machines want him gone. Worst dealmaker in Valoria. Indictments don't stock shelves, folks. Elect a businessman. Fire the prosecutor.

Arithmetic error? Darling, I watched Rostova raise interest rates at donor dinners while mothers skipped dinner. Her austerity is the real gouging — cold spreadsheets, cold heart, empty carts. Eliminate the error.

Beloved, Rostova governs the arithmetic while Valoria's mothers weep over empty baskets! Twelve-dollar eggs? She calls it discipline—I call it a cold heart in a cold spreadsheet! Cast out this winter of the soul!

General, I freed eighty hostages without firing a bullet — you'd spend ten thousand. Vance brings rifles to a grocery crisis; you can't shell a supermarket. His bravado starves families. Read the room, Valoria — retire him.

Haddon's response to twelve-dollar eggs? Prayer — an unverified protocol with zero efficacy data. Fifteen million souls, one luxury jet, empty baskets. His platform is emotional malware infecting the national cortex. Purge it.

Colleagues, Garrick Stone's proud résumé is simply a list of enemies — governors, oligarchs, entire party machines. Consensus feeds families; feuds fill headlines. Valoria deserves a builder, not a bomb-thrower with a subpoena. Retire the prosecutor.

Sterling claims indictments don't stock shelves? Exhibit A: his shell-company grocery mergers doubled your bill overnight. He'd run Valoria like a Fortune 500—workers get fired first. Jury of Valoria: fire Arthur Sterling.
